questionText:

SkyHigh Airlines Ltd. spent six months and Rs. 5 Crore on external management consulting to formulate a rigid 5-year global expansion plan. The detailed plan prescribed flight routes, crew hiring, and long-term jet fuel procurement contracts. However, two unforeseen external shocks struck simultaneously: global crude oil prices surged by 80% due to geopolitical warfare, and a foreign exchange currency crisis depreciated the home currency, escalating aircraft lease costs. When regional route managers noticed passenger demand collapsing on international sectors, they requested permission to re-route aircraft to lucrative domestic tier-2 routes. The executive committee refused, insisting that operational managers must adhere strictly to the approved 5-year master document ('Planning leads to rigidity'). Furthermore, lower-level managers stopped thinking creatively, waiting mechanically for head-office instructions ('Planning reduces creativity'). Hence Option C is correct.
